chapter_title: The Chapter of the Nazorean who questions the Teacher
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a late debate-frame (Nazorean interlocutor + ‘apostle’ dialogue) and ethical-judicial argumentation rather than systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential exposition. The only explicit scriptural overlay is the Gospel saying about treasure/heart (Mt 6:21), and adjacent eschatological vocabulary (“gehenna”, “life eternal”) likely belongs to the same Christian-lexical stratum. No recoverable oldest correspondential substrate is present.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening (‘Once again, it happened one time’) and hagiographic dialogue setup with ‘apostle’ title mark compilation frame, not substrate teaching.
Dialogue-attribution (‘The apostle speaks to him’) and rhetorical negotiation about ‘single word’ belongs to narrative/frame apparatus.
Interlocutor’s trap-question (‘good or evil?’) functions as polemical dialogue content; no cosmological/correspondential system is being expounded.

Contains explicit dialogue attribution and polemical repartee; the ‘A judge is my God’ line is embedded in the debated-story register rather than an impersonal cosmological degree-map characteristic of the oldest layer.
Extended objection speech framed as a city-court analogy (‘lashes… racks… sword’) continues the constructed debate narrative; not a cosmos→cosmos correspondence sequence.

Ethical/theodicy-style explanation of punishment as limiting evil; argumentative moral reasoning rather than systematic cosmological architecture. Still cast as direct address within the debate scene.
Application/exhortation voice (‘pay attention to this’) and moral reassurance about the innocent before the judge; this is behavioral-ethical instruction, not substrate cosmology.
Continues the moral logic of retribution/recompense (‘brings his sin… upon his own head’; ‘paid recompense’). Ethics without cosmological mechanism → pastoral layer.

Applies the judge-analogy directly to God (‘judge of souls’) with moral alternatives (obey devil vs truth/knowledge). The fragmentary ending prevents firmer dating, but the register remains ethical-judicial, not correspondential substrate.
Explicit Gospel-citation formula (‘Even as the saviour has said… Where your heart is…’) makes the whole paragraph Christian overlay, regardless of any internal correspondential quality.

Eschatological condemnation language culminating in ‘gehenna of burning’ aligns with NT/Gospel vocabulary; likely enters through Christian lexical overlay even without an explicit citation formula here.

Reward-for-good-deeds eschatology with ‘heirs’ and ‘life eternal’ is strongly Christian-lexical; ‘kingdom of light’ is Manichaean-compatible, but the phrasing reads as Christianized reward discourse, so treated as overlay.
Concluding moral summation (‘you see God… is a judge… limits the evil’) in exhortative-demonstrative voice; no cosmological degree-structure or internal correspondence mapping.
